entries.post:
$176M went into US spot Bitcoin ETFs on Tuesday. Two funds took all of it.

IBIT: +$151.5M
FBTC: +$24.5M
The other 10 funds: zero.

One day of $BTC ETF flows tells you shares were created. Not who bought or why.

Do you track flows daily or weekly?

entries.topic: 'Uptober' falla otra vez: $BTC va camino a su segundo octubre negativo seguido
entries.why: Tema estacional que todos comentan a fin de mes. Ángulo quant propio: tabla de retornos de octubre con datos reales; invita a debatir si la estacionalidad sirve.
entries.post:
Uptober didn't show up. Again.

$BTC October returns (monthly open to close):
2019: +10.3%
2020: +28.0%
2021: +39.9%
2022: +5.5%
2023: +28.5%
2024: +11.0%
2025: -3.9%
2026 so far: -2.7%

Six green Octobers, then two red ones.

Seasonality is a tendency, not a promise. And one weak month doesn't tell you much about the next twelve.

Do you still look at monthly seasonality?
cta: Bookmark this and check it again on November 1.
If it was useful, a repost helps more people see it.

entries.topic: Falsa 'Trust Wallet Card' ($1, 8% cashback, límite $100.000, sin KYC) vacía wallets vía aprobaciones de tokens
entries.why: Seguridad práctica y accionable; encaja con la línea de custodia de la cuenta. Checklist corto = bookmarks y reposts.
entries.post:
A $1 crypto card with 8% cashback, a $100,000 limit and no KYC.

It's a fake site using Trust Wallet's brand. Trust Wallet's security team confirmed it's not theirs.

The trap isn't the $1. It's the step where you connect your wallet and sign an approval. That can let a contract move your tokens. No seed phrase needed.

3 habits:
• Only use the official app and site
• Use a separate wallet for connecting to sites
• Review and revoke old token approvals

Which one do you actually do?
cta: A repost might keep someone from signing the wrong thing.

entries.topic: Strategy no compró BTC (19-25 oct): usó $204.9M en recomprar su preferente STRC; mantiene 848.517 BTC
entries.why: Cambio de comportamiento del mayor tenedor corporativo, con cifras del 8-K (verificables). Genera debate sin necesidad de exagerar.
entries.post:
Strategy had cash last week. It didn't buy Bitcoin.

Oct 19-25, per its 8-K:
• $204.9M spent buying back its own STRC preferred stock
• 0 BTC bought or sold
• Holdings: 848,517 BTC, avg cost ~$75,446
• USD Cash left: $242.4M

When the largest corporate $BTC holder spends on its own capital structure, that's worth reading carefully. It's not a sale. It's also not a bid.

Pause or pattern? The next 8-K will say more.

entries.topic: Itaú, primer banco de Brasil en formalizar ante el Banco Central su intermediación y custodia cripto (Resolución 520, plazo 30/10)
entries.why: Adopción en LatAm, cercana a la audiencia hispana. Ángulo propio: custodia bancaria vs. tener tus llaves.
entries.post:
Brazil's largest private bank just put its Bitcoin custody on the record.

Itaú Unibanco notified the central bank of its crypto trading and custody services under the new rules (Resolution 520). It's the first bank to do it. The deadline is Oct 30.

It offers 15 assets, including $BTC, and has since Dec 2023. It doesn't disclose users or volumes.

Bank custody makes access easier. It's still someone else holding the keys.

Would you hold $BTC at your bank?
cta: Bookmark this if you're comparing custody options.

entries.topic: Búsquedas de 'bitcoin' en Google en mínimos de ~5 años con el precio cerca de $81k
entries.why: Contraste fuerte (precio alto vs. interés bajo) que genera debate. Ángulo diferenciado: la demanda migró a ETFs y apps, la métrica vieja puede engañar.
entries.post:
Almost nobody is Googling Bitcoin. $BTC is still near $81k.

Worldwide search interest just hit 19 out of 100, the lowest reading in five years of weekly data.

But a lot of people now buy through an ETF or a broker app. They don't search anything first.

Maybe the old metric just measures less than it used to.

entries.topic: Caída bajo $80k liquidó más de $200M en apuestas apalancadas en una hora
entries.why: Encaja con la postura de la cuenta (spot, sin apalancamiento). Contenido educativo con alto potencial de bookmarks.
entries.post:
$200M+ got liquidated in one hour when $BTC lost $80k.

The price moved a few percent. Spot holders didn't lose a single coin.

Leverage doesn't change your thesis. It changes how long you get to hold it.

entries.topic: Franklin Templeton presenta ETFs que reinvierten dividendos de acciones en Bitcoin (FBEQ, FIBT)
entries.why: Noticia de adopción con mecánica concreta y explicable. Buen hilo corto educativo.
entries.post:
What if your dividends bought Bitcoin on their own?

Franklin Templeton filed two ETFs with the SEC (FBEQ and FIBT): 95% stocks, 5% $BTC, with dividends reinvested into Bitcoin. Rebalance target 5%, hard cap 20%.

It's passive exposure without touching an exchange. Just remember: exposure isn't custody.

entries.topic: Galaxy Research dice que el bear market terminó en junio; nivel a vigilar: media de 50 semanas ~$76.5k
entries.why: Debate fuerte (Calacanis vs Saylor/Galaxy). Ángulo quant: un nivel concreto que invalida la tesis, en vez de opinión.
entries.post:
Galaxy says the Bitcoin bear market ended in June.

The useful part isn't the claim. It's the line that tests it: the 50-week moving average, now about $76k on weekly closes.

Above it, the thesis holds. Below it, $BTC has something to prove.

entries.topic: Datavault AI: 817.6 BTC atrapados en un exchange 4 meses; acciones −49.6% y reexpresión de estados financieros
entries.why: Caso real y verificable (SEC filing) que encaja perfecto con la postura de custodia de la cuenta. Alto potencial de bookmarks y reposts; ángulo educativo, no burla.
entries.post:
A public company thought it owned 817.6 BTC. It couldn't withdraw a single one.

Datavault AI says the coins have been stuck in an exchange wallet since June, despite repeated withdrawal requests. It's now restating four quarters of financials. Shares fell 49.6% in a day.

Owning $BTC and controlling $BTC are not the same thing. Learn how custody works before you size up.
cta: Bookmark this before you leave coins on an exchange.
A repost might save someone a hard lesson.

entries.topic: ETFs spot de BTC: +$110.3M netos el 26/10, 100% de IBIT (BlackRock); el resto en cero
entries.why: Dato concreto de flujos con contraste (un solo fondo explica todo). Encaja con la serie de 'quién compra mientras el retail no busca'.
entries.post:
One fund did all the buying.

On October 26, US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $110.3M net. Every dollar went to BlackRock's IBIT, roughly 1,380 BTC. The other Bitcoin ETFs had zero net flow.

Retail searches are at lows, but institutional demand for $BTC hasn't gone quiet. Concentration in one fund is worth watching too.
cta: Bookmark this if you track ETF flows.
